result.description:
Unlike most support work, this isn't shifts in a facility. At Like Family, you choose your own clients, set your own hours, and work close to home - spending real time with people in their community, doing things they enjoy.

And here's the good part: getting started has never been easier. Download the Like Family app, build your profile as you go, and you could be activated and booking your first job within 24 hours.


What makes Like Family different
- You're called a Social Carer - because it's about connection, not just tasks
- You pick your clients and your schedule - no rostering, no mandatory shifts
- Work local: get matched with people in your own suburb
- No experience required - we'll set you up with a full induction
- Be part of a community of carers, not just a workforce on an app

What you'll actually do
- Join clients on outings - movies, beaches, markets, sport, concerts, fishing
- Be a companion: reduce loneliness and help people feel included in their community
- Help with skill-building (e.g. using public transport, cooking, budgeting)
- Assist with meal prep, light exercise and healthy routines
- Help with errands, appointments and getting around
- Light household tasks like cleaning and gardening
- If you choose: personal care support (toileting, showering, mobility, medication) at higher rates

Who we're looking for
We welcome all backgrounds. If you're patient, reliable and genuinely enjoy spending time with people - you're already most of the way there.
Great with people who have: Autism (ASD), ADHD, Anxiety, Depression, PTSD, Schizophrenia, Intellectual Disability, Chronic Pain, Aged Care needs, Developmental Delay

What you need (minimum)
- Right to work in Australia + 100 points of ID
- Australian Business Number (ABN) - or willingness to obtain one (easy to set up, we'll show you how)
- NDIS Worker Screening Check or Police Check - or willingness to get one

Nice to have - but not required to start
- Cert III/IV in Individual Support, Disability or Aged Care
- Driver's licence and valid vehicle registration
- First Aid Certificate
- Working With Children Check
- Experience in mental health, nursing or community services

Pay info: 

Social Care:
Weekdays: $46/hour
Weekends & public holidays: $63/hour

Personal Care:
Weekdays: $50/hour
Weekends & public holidays: $67/hour

What you can expect
- Flexibility: Choose your clients, your hours, and work close to home - there’s no fixed roster.
- Support: Our team is here to help you succeed, plus a carer community to connect with.
- Competitive pay: Above-market rates, weekend loading, and bonus rates for multiple clients.
- Purpose: Meaningful work that genuinely reduces loneliness - you'll see the difference you make.

How to apply - the fastest way in is the app
Skip the back-and-forth. Download the Like Family app - search "Like Family" on the App Store or Google Play - and get started today.

1. Download the app and create your profile. Your profile builds as you go, so setup feels effortless - no long forms, no waiting around.
2. Get verified - we'll guide you through your ABN and Worker Screening/Police Check if you don't already have them.
3. Get activated - most carers are up and running within 24 hours.
4. Start booking jobs - everything you need is in one place, so you can start meeting local clients and earning straight away.

Want to know more about the application process first? Head to likefamily.com.au/support-worker-jobs to see what being a Like Family Social Carer really looks like.

Join thousands of carers earning flexible income doing work that genuinely makes a difference.

Like Family - enjoying life together. We're building a community where carers and clients genuinely connect. If that sounds like you, we'd love to have you.

Our client, Highflow Connections Pty Ltd, is a leading provider of NBN installation, repair, and maintenance services. Conveniently located in Hurstville, NSW, the company specializes in delivering reliable and efficient telecommunications solutions, including installation processes, network outages management, device compatibility, and ongoing repair and maintenance services.

With a commitment to excellence and customer satisfaction, Highflow Connections ensures that its clients receive top-tier support to stay connected. Utilizing advanced technologies and a highly skilled workforce, the company plays a vital role in shaping Australia's telecommunications infrastructure.

Highflow Connections is seeking a dedicated Telecommunications Cable Jointer, and, in this role, you will be responsible for joining, terminating, and repairing copper and fibre optic cables. Your work will ensure that telecommunications networks remain operational and meet the highest standards of quality and reliability.

The ideal candidate will possess a strong technical background, hands-on experience in cable jointing, and a commitment to maintaining the integrity of telecommunications networks. You will work collaboratively with a team of skilled technicians to provide uninterrupted connectivity for clients.

Qualifications and Experience Requirements:

-	A Certificate IV in Telecommunications Technology or equivalent qualification.
-	At least one year experience in telecommunications cable jointing or a related field.

Key Tasks and Responsibilities:

-	Join, terminate, and repair copper and fibre optic telecommunications cables
-	Attach wires and cables to appliances and telecommunications devices.
-	Test and troubleshoot equipment using electronic instruments to identify faults.
-	Adjust, replace, and repair defective items to ensure network reliability.
-	Seal cable sheaths using lead and thermoplastic materials to protect against environmental factors.
-	Install and maintain aerial and underground wires and cables for telecommunication networks.
-	Erect and test support structures for overhead cable installations.
-	Perform regular inspections and maintenance of telecommunications systems to prevent outages.
-	Ensure all work complies with industry standards, safety protocols, and client specifications.
-	Assist in the installation of telecommunications equipment, including modems and routers.
-	Document work activities, including repairs and installations, for reporting and record-keeping.
-	Collaborate with team members to ensure timely completion of projects.

Skills Requirements:

-	Strong technical and diagnostic skills in telecommunications systems.
-	Familiarity with copper and fibre optic cables, including jointing and termination techniques.
-	Strong understanding of industry standards, safety practices, and regulatory requirements.
-	Physical fitness and the ability to work in confined spaces or at heights.
-	Proficiency in using cable jointing and termination tools and equipment.
-	Excellent problem-solving abilities to address network issues effectively.
-	Effective communication skills for liaising with team members and clients.

If you are a skilled Telecommunications Cable Jointer with a passion for ensuring seamless connectivity, we want to hear from you! 

Please send your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au

Job Description:
The Analyst Programmer is responsible for designing, developing, testing, and maintaining software applications that support business objectives. Key duties include writing and reviewing code, conducting software testing, and ensuring that application functionality meets specified requirements. The role also involves researching and designing technical solutions, as well as documenting and updating software specifications throughout the development lifecycle.
Responsibilities:
Demonstrate a strong understanding of coding methods, industry best practices, and software development standards.
Conduct interviews with end-users to gather insights into functionality, interface issues, usability, and challenges, ensuring user needs are effectively addressed.
Develop comprehensive test cases and test plans to ensure the reliability and performance of software applications.
Stay informed on data privacy laws and practices to ensure software development remains compliant.
Communicate clearly with non-technical staff and collaborate effectively across multidisciplinary teams.
Embrace new technologies and maintain a commitment to ongoing learning and skill development.
Display excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills to convey ideas and requirements effectively.
Conduct research into software-related challenges and assess potential solutions or products.
Demonstrate initiative, autonomy, and direction in executing work tasks and delivering projects.
Maintain strong attention to detail, ensuring accuracy and precision throughout the development process.
Apply analytical and problem-solving skills to resolve complex software-related issues.
Manage task prioritisation and execute effectively under pressure to meet project deadlines.
Collaborate closely with developers, programmers, and designers to conceptualise and develop innovative software solutions.
Evaluate existing business systems and processes to identify optimisation opportunities.
Assist in gathering, defining, and documenting business requirements, deliverables, and specifications in partnership with internal departments.
Contribute to software development project planning, including scope definition, scheduling, and implementation.
Engage with internal and external programme users to understand and fulfil functional requirements.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
At least 2 years of hands-on experience working as an Analyst Programmer or in a similar software development role.
Proficient in one or more programming languages such as Java, C#, Python, or JavaScript.
Strong understanding of database concepts and practical experience writing and optimising SQL queries.
Experience developing web applications using technologies such as HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Angular, or ASP.NET.
Familiarity with modern software development methodologies, including Agile and Scrum frameworks.
Sound knowledge of software testing principles, with exposure to tools like JUnit or Selenium.
Experience using version control systems such as Git or SVN, and project tracking tools like JIRA or Trello.
Understanding of cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure, along with their core services and deployment models.
Solid foundation in object-oriented programming (OOP) and commonly used software design patterns.
Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills, with the ability to identify and resolve complex coding issues.
Effective communicator with the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams and stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to manage tasks, prioritise deliverables, and meet project deadlines.
Self-motivated with a commitment to ongoing learning and staying current with emerging tools and technologies.
Permanent Residents (PR) and Australian Citizens are eligible to apply
Job Types: Full-time, Permanent
Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super
Benefits: Work from home
Schedule: 8-hour shift

FORMWORK CARPENTER 
KWIK FORMWORK
JANDAKOT, PERTH WA 6164 
FULL-TIME PERMANENT

Position Overview
As a Formwork Carpenter at KWIK FORMWORK, you will play a pivotal role in the construction, erection, and installation of formwork for various structures on key projects. This position requires a skilled tradesperson with leadership abilities to ensure the successful completion of tasks while maintaining high standards of safety and quality.

Key Responsibilities
•	Review and Interpret Plans: Carefully review and interpret project plans and blueprints to identify the materials needed, dimensions, and the best installation approach.
•	Material Selection and Planning: Select and order the necessary materials and prepare detailed layouts for the formwork construction process.
•	Construct, Erect, and Install Formwork: Execute precise measurements and work from technical drawings to create and set up formwork for concrete structures.
•	Installation of Cladding and Fixtures: Install fascia panels, roof sheathing, and fit exterior cladding, along with door and window frames, to complete the formwork.
•	Maintenance and Repairs: Carry out repairs on existing formwork and structures as needed, ensuring they remain functional and up to standard.
•	Versatile Material Handling: Work with a range of materials, including laminates, Perspex, and metals, as required by the project.
•	Lead and Supervise: Oversee a team of formwork carpenters, ensuring tasks are completed efficiently and to a high standard.
•	Safety Compliance: Adhere to and enforce safety protocols on-site, ensuring a safe working environment for all team members.
•	Quality Control: Inspect and verify the quality of the formwork installation, ensuring it meets project specifications and industry standards.
•	Collaboration: Work closely with project managers, engineers, and other trades to coordinate and streamline the construction process.
•	Problem-Solving: Identify and address any issues that arise during the formwork installation process, finding effective solutions to keep the project on track.
•	Training and Mentoring: Provide guidance and training to less experienced team members, fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

Qualifications and Skills
•	Cert III Equivalent & Experience: This position requires a Certificate III equivalent or a minimum of 3 years’ experience in the trade.
•	Industry Knowledge: Demonstrated industry knowledge is essential for this position.
•	WA Building and Construction Industry Card: A current WA Building and Construction Industry White/Blue Card is mandatory.
•	Technical Proficiency: Ability to read and interpret drawings accurately.
•	High-Rise Experience: Prior experience in high-rise construction is highly desirable.

Shape the future of complex engineering programs in a high-visibility configuration management role.   
   An innovative and growing Australian engineering organisation is seeking an experienced Configuration Manager to lead, mature and continuously improve configuration management across complex systems, equipment and software programs. This is a hands-on, high-impact opportunity for someone who enjoys building structure, driving governance and partnering closely with engineering, project and delivery teams.   
   
  Your New Company  
   
 This is a rare opportunity to join a forward-thinking engineering business with a strong reputation for technical excellence, innovation and long-term project delivery. Based in a beautiful location, the organisation offers the best of both worlds: meaningful, visible project work within a supportive environment that values collaboration, capability uplift and career development. 
   
 You will be surrounded by excellent leadership and mentorship, with genuine access to senior decision-makers, clear progression pathways and the opportunity to make your mark on projects that matter. 
   
  Your New Role  
   
 As Configuration Manager, you will take ownership of the configuration management framework across complex engineering programs. This role blends strategic governance with practical delivery, giving you the autonomy to shape processes while remaining close to the technical detail. 
 
 Own, maintain and continuously improve configuration management policies, processes, procedures and tools. 
 Establish and govern configuration baselines across the full system lifecycle. 
 Lead configuration control activities, including Change Control Boards. 
 Manage engineering change processes, configuration status accounting and configuration audits. 
 Maintain accurate configuration records, drawings, specifications and associated technical data. 
 Provide practical CM guidance to engineering, project and delivery teams. 
 Support compliance with relevant defence, engineering and industry standards. 
 
  What You'll Need to Succeed  
 
 Significant configuration management experience within defence, aerospace or complex engineering environments. 
 Experience developing and implementing CM frameworks, policies and procedures. 
 Strong understanding of configuration data, baselines and engineering change processes. 
 Knowledge of relevant CM standards such as EIA-649, MIL-HDBK-61, ISO, ITIL or equivalent. 
 Hands-on experience using CM or PLM tools; Windchill experience will be highly regarded. 
 Ability to operate strategically while also supporting hands-on delivery. 
 Strong stakeholder engagement skills across technical and project teams. 
 A degree in Engineering, Systems Engineering, IT or a related discipline. 
 
  What's in it for you  
 
 Excellent leadership, mentorship and support from experienced senior leaders. 
 Clear progression opportunities within a growing and highly visible organisation. 
 Exposure to complex, meaningful engineering projects with genuine technical depth. 
 The chance to shape and improve configuration management capability from the ground up. 
 A collaborative, innovative and dynamic working environment. 
 Beautiful location with access to an enviable lifestyle and engaging project work. 
 Strong company visibility, where your contribution will be recognised and valued. 
 
  What to do now:  
   
 If you are a hands-on Configuration Manager looking for a role with autonomy, visibility, mentorship and long-term career growth, this is an opportunity worth exploring. 
   
 Apply now or send your CV directly to Amy McNulty directly at   amy.mcnulty@hays.com.au    
     Please  click here  to apply.

The Stonemason is responsible for constructing, repairing, and installing stone structures, retaining walls, masonry features, and related stonework in accordance with project specifications and construction requirements.
This is a full-time position with an annual salary of $80,000 to $90,000 plus superannuation. 

The Responsibilities
•	Cut and shape hard and soft stone blocks and masonry slabs to construct and renovate stone structures, kitchen benchtops, and monumental masonry
•	Lay pre-cut stones and masonry blocks in mortar to construct and repair walls, partitions, arches, and structural stone features
•	Study plans and specifications to determine material requirements, dimensions, and installation procedures
•	Erect and dismantle restricted height scaffolding in accordance with workplace safety procedures
•	Seal foundations with damp-resistant materials and apply mortar layers to support masonry installation works
•	Lay stones in rows, designs, and patterns while maintaining structural alignment and finish quality
•	Embed stone blocks in mortar and remove excess material to achieve clean and accurate finishes
•	Check vertical and horizontal alignment of stone structures using levelling and measuring equipment
•	Cut, shape, polish, and finish stone materials using hand tools, polishing equipment, and masonry machinery
•	Repair and maintain stone, brick, and masonry structures in accordance with construction requirements
•	Design, cut, and install monumental masonry and stone lettering works
•	Construct retaining walls, stone facades, and structural masonry installations for residential and commercial projects Choose and prepare appropriate metal materials for fabrication

The Requirements
•	Certificate III in Stonemasonry, Bricklaying, Construction, or equivalent trade qualification
•	Minimum 5 years’ experience as a Stonemason within construction, landscaping, or masonry environments
•	Minimum 5 years’ experience interpreting technical drawings, specifications, and construction measurements for masonry works
•	At least 5 years’ experience constructing retaining walls, stone structures, and masonry installations across residential or commercial projects
•	At least 5 years’ experience operating masonry tools, polishing equipment, cutting machinery, and stone fabrication tools
•	At least 5 years’ experience constructing stone retaining walls, rock walls, garden walls, paving, steps and outdoor stone features
•	Minimum 5 years’ experience using stone cutting, grinding, drilling, shaping and finishing tools in a construction or landscaping environment
•	Strong knowledge of masonry construction methods, mortar application, and stone finishing techniques
•	Ability to read and interpret technical plans, site measurements, and installation specifications accurately
•	Strong understanding of workplace safety procedures, scaffolding requirements, and construction compliance standards
•	White Card required
•	Excavator and Skid Steer licences preferred
•	Ability to work outdoors, at heights, and across varying construction site environments
•	Strong work ethic, reliability, and ability to work independently or within construction teams
•	High attention to detail and commitment to workmanship quality
